comparison: Both evaluate the orthogonality of SF and color domains (C41-C44, C60, C63). OpenEval finds the claims SUPPORTED with appropriate statistical tests. Peer reviewers are UNCERTAIN, calling results 'too good to be true' and requesting additional controls, statistical analyses, and presentation of all regions rather than selected examples. Concerns about potential systematic distortion and the cocktail blank method are raised.

Both evaluate area-specific SF preferences (C17-C19, C67). OpenEval finds claims SUPPORTED with appropriate statistical analysis. Peer reviewers also find this SUPPORTED, acknowledging 'the differences look clear,' though they request additional statistical analysis and note the finding is 'unremarkable' as it replicates known results.

Both evaluate the relationship between SF and color domains (C45, C47, C61). OpenEval rates this UNCERTAIN due to lack of statistical significance and small sample size, though notes a consistent trend. Peer reviewers rate this UNSUPPORTED, explicitly rejecting the claim as inadequately supported and recommending elimination of these analyses due to weak relationships and lack of significance.

Both evaluate periodic SF variation in V2 (C48-C49, C53-C55, C71). OpenEval finds the periodic variation SUPPORTED but notes C56 is speculative. Peer reviewers find this UNSUPPORTED, stating that establishing periodicity requires statistical analysis and that the visible V2 region is insufficient to distinguish CO stripes from other patterns. They request Fourier analysis and recommend eliminating these claims.

OpenEval R6 evaluates systematic spatial shifts in activation patterns (C20-C26) and finds them SUPPORTED. Peer R2 evaluates overlapping claims about topographic organization (C21, C25, C33, C57-C58, C68, C74) but is UNCERTAIN, raising concerns about the centroid analysis methodology, lack of statistical analysis, and recommending de-emphasis as a main result.

Both evaluate eccentricity-dependent SF processing differences (C27-C30 overlap). OpenEval finds these claims SUPPORTED by quantitative analysis. Peer R6 covers broader claims (C20-C40, C59, C69-C70) and finds them SUPPORTED, though with implicit acceptance rather than explicit endorsement. The lack of specific criticism suggests acceptance of these observations.

OpenEval R8 evaluates V1 foveal SF preferences (C31-C34) and finds them SUPPORTED. Peer R6 includes these claims (C31-C32) within a broader set and rates them SUPPORTED, though the evaluation focuses more on the overall topographic findings rather than these specific V1 observations.

OpenEval R9 evaluates correlation analysis of regional SF differences (C35-C37) and finds them SUPPORTED. Peer R6 includes these claims within a broader evaluation and rates them SUPPORTED, though without explicit discussion of the correlation analysis specifically.

OpenEval R10 evaluates inferences about V4 foveal SF sensitivity (C38-C40) and finds them SUPPORTED as reasonable inferences. Peer R6 includes these claims and rates them SUPPORTED, though notes one reviewer suggests considering how this relates to 3D shape from shading tuning in V4.

OpenEval R14 evaluates the three major findings summary (C57-C61) and finds them SUPPORTED. Peer R2 includes C57-C58 in their evaluation of topographic claims and rates them UNCERTAIN due to methodological concerns about the centroid analysis and lack of statistical rigor.

Both include C61 (major finding about SF-color relationship). OpenEval finds the summary SUPPORTED as accurately representing findings. Peer reviewers find the underlying evidence UNSUPPORTED and recommend eliminating these claims, creating a fundamental disagreement about this major conclusion.

Both evaluate the orthogonality principle and its generalizability (C62-C66, C75-C76, C79-C80, C84). OpenEval finds these SUPPORTED with some speculation about generalizability. Peer reviewers are UNCERTAIN because the interpretive claims depend on the orthogonality findings, which they question. While the public review calls evidence 'convincing,' detailed critiques challenge the empirical basis.

Both evaluate the general model and theoretical framework (C74-C81 overlap with C75-C76, C79-C80, C84). OpenEval finds the synthesis SUPPORTED but notes speculation about evolutionary origins. Peer reviewers are UNCERTAIN because the broader theoretical framework depends on the questioned orthogonality findings, though the framework itself is not directly critiqued.

Both include C67 (V4 SF preferences). OpenEval finds claims about V4 SF processing SUPPORTED and consistent with prior work. Peer reviewers also find this SUPPORTED, though note it replicates known results and is 'unremarkable.'

Both include C71 (V2 periodic SF variation). OpenEval finds C71 SUPPORTED by experimental observations. Peer reviewers find this UNSUPPORTED, stating the periodicity claim is not well quantified and requires Fourier analysis to establish.

OpenEval evaluates foundational context claims from prior research (C1-C5) and finds them SUPPORTED. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, as reviewers focused on novel findings rather than background literature summary.

OpenEval evaluates V2 organization knowledge from literature (C6-C9) and finds them SUPPORTED. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, as these represent background context rather than novel claims.

OpenEval evaluates V4 functional organization from literature (C10-C13) and finds them SUPPORTED. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, as these establish background knowledge rather than new findings.

OpenEval evaluates the study's testable predictions (C14-C16) and finds them SUPPORTED as clear hypotheses. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, as reviewers focused on results rather than hypothesis formulation.

OpenEval evaluates claims about parallel processing streams (C82-C84) and finds them SUPPORTED with some speculation. Peer R7 includes C84 but focuses on the broader theoretical framework rather than these specific processing stream claims.

OpenEval evaluates methodological details (C85-C88) and finds them SUPPORTED with adequate description. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, as reviewers did not critique the basic methodological descriptions.
